title: introduce imageMirror and rollbackQuarantine values + overlay transformer for private installs
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add new .Values.imageMirror and .Values.rollbackQuarantine controls for private installs; introduce an overlay-transformer helper to apply lightweight kustomize-like overlays from values; add economy-mode scheduling for non-critical initJobs to reduce burst resource usage during upgrades; no user-facing API breaking changes, opt-in via values.
body: Context and motivation: Private on-prem and airgapped installs frequently require mirrored images, deterministic upgrade/rollback behavior, and lightweight value-driven templating so operators can adapt charts without full retemplating. This PR introduces three related capabilities: (1) .Values.imageMirror - a declarative way to rewrite image references for airgapped registries and per-namespace mirrors, (2) .Values.rollbackQuarantine - an optional quarantine namespace and marker that keeps pre-upgrade workloads readable for forensic rollback while preventing accidental routing, and (3) an overlay-transformer helper that applies simple value-driven overlays (patches) to Deployment/DaemonSet manifests without introducing a full kustomize runtime in the installer. Summary of changes: - Add values.schema.json entries for imageMirror and rollbackQuarantine with validation and examples. - Implement template helpers in _helpers.tpl for image rewriting and overlay application. - Add a new chart helper overlay-transformer.yaml that renders annotated strategic merge patches when overlay values are present. - Introduce 'initScheduler.economyMode' which defers non-critical initJobs via a backoff/jitter schedule for upgrades to avoid simultaneous heavy init bursts. - Add upgrade hooks that honor rollbackQuarantine: when enabled, upgrade creates quarantined copies of affected Deployments and Services with a quarantine label and explicit networkPolicy to block external traffic. - Document migration steps and CLI examples for private-installer (helm --set imageMirror.*). Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by infra and security (ENG-1265) - [x] Values schema validated with helm plugin test harness - [x] Unit template tests for helper functions - [x] Manual airgap install test against mirrored registry - [x] Upgrade/rollback canary tested on ci-cluster Implementation notes: The imageMirror config supports three rewrite strategies in values: exactMap (map original->mirror), prefixReplace (rewrite registry prefix), and registryFallback (list of fallback registries to try in order). The image helper resolves images in this priority order and sets imagePullSecrets if mirror registry requires credentials and credentials are provided under .Values.imageMirror.credentials.<registry>. The overlay-transformer is intentionally limited: it supports patching container.env, resources, nodeSelectors, and annotations. Those patches are emitted as Kubernetes patch resources with annotations that the installer uses to apply with kubectl patch or server-side apply depending on the deployment mode. The rollbackQuarantine flow: when enabled, during a helm upgrade the chart emits a PreUpgrade hook that copies selected resources into the quarantine namespace with suffix -quarantine-<timestamp>, labels them with redwood.rollback/quarantine=true and attaches a generated NetworkPolicy that isolates the objects. A PostUpgrade hook removes quarantine resources after the rollout window or when explicit --release-quarantine=false is set. Rollback will automatically prefer quarantine snapshots to improve rollback determinism. Backwards compatibility: all features are opt-in and default to disabled. Existing installs are unaffected unless operators set the new values. Testing: template unit tests added under tests/templates/*, integration check in ci uses a mocked mirror registry and validates rewrite behavior, upgrade canary executed on a small cluster with economyMode enabled to confirm initJobs are serialized. Migration / operator guidance: examples in docs/values-examples/airgap.md and an upgrade checklist added to docs/upgrades/rollback-quarantine.md. Commands: helm upgrade my-release redwood/private --set imageMirror.prefixReplace="mirror.corp.registry/" --set rollbackQuarantine.enabled=true Please see commits and file list for details and small snippets of the new helpers.

merge_commit_message: introduce imageMirror, rollbackQuarantine, and overlay transformer for private installs\n\nAdds opt-in image mirroring, a quarantine flow for safer rollbacks, lightweight overlay transformer helper, and an economy-mode initScheduler to reduce upgrade resource spikes. See docs/ and tests/ for examples and verification steps. Resolves ENG-1265.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior is zero-change. To opt-in for airgapped installs: helm upgrade --set imageMirror.prefixReplace="mirror.corp.registry/" --set rollbackQuarantine.enabled=true. If using private registries that require credentials, populate .Values.imageMirror.credentials.<registry>.secretName and ensure the secret exists in the target namespace. Quarantine TTL default 72h can be tuned via .Values.rollbackQuarantine.ttl. Economy mode for init jobs is disabled by default and can be enabled with .Values.initScheduler.economyMode.enabled=true.
security_implications: Quarantine snapshots are isolated by NetworkPolicy by default and do not bind external ClusterIP Services. Image rewrite supports credentialed mirrors; credentials must be supplied by operators. Added validation to values.schema.json to avoid accidental plaintext credential fields. Security team reviewed and sign-off recorded under ENG-1265.
testing_instructions: Unit test: run make test-templates. Integration: deploy a small cluster with mock mirror registry, helm upgrade with imageMirror set, validate pods pull from mirror, enable rollbackQuarantine and trigger upgrade, verify quarantine namespace and resources created and isolated. See docs/upgrades/rollback-quarantine.md for step-by-step commands.
